claims.text: Let \(q=n-r\), assume \(a=1,b=2\), and use the accepted integral Schur/Pieri presentation \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\). Then \(i,j\ge2\), \(q-i,r-j\ge1\), \(\min(i,j)=2\), and \(\min(q-i,r-j)=1\).

Put \[ x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}, \] \[ y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},\quad y_2=s_{(i^j,2)}. \] In \(Q\), Pieri relations give \[ \bar x_1+\bar y_1=0,\qquad \bar u+\bar x_2+\bar z=0,\qquad \bar u+\bar z+\bar y_2=0, \] where \(u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})}\) is interpreted as \(0\) if outside the \(q^r\)-box and \(z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)}\). Hence \[ \bar y_1=-\bar x_1,\qquad \bar y_2=\bar x_2. \]

Consequently the two \(a=1,b=2\) proposed families \[ F_1=(x_0,x_1,x_2),\qquad F_2=(x_0,y_1,y_2) \] have images related in \(Q\) by the unimodular diagonal matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)\). Thus either family is an integral basis of its span in \(Q\) exactly when the other is.

**Uniform \(a=1,b=2\) elimination lemma.** In the accepted integral presentation of \(Q\), all Schur columns other than \(x_0,x_1,x_2\) admit integral unit-pivot elimination, with no residual relation on these three columns. Equivalently, \[ Q\cong\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2. \]
